story.headline: Dried on farmer rooftops in Dusun Gura, Buntu Mondong.
story.p1: COGURA takes its name from Dusun Gura in Buntu Mondong Village, Buntu Batu District, an old Kalosi Arabica farming hamlet on the slopes of Mount Latimojong where families have grown coffee since the 1750s. At 1,300-1,600m ASL with 17-19°C daytime air and iron-rich volcanic soil, farmers tend shade-grown trees using the local Sistem Pekon tradition with minimal synthetic inputs.
story.p2: Walk through Buntu Mondong and you will notice something unusual: families build extra upper roofs on top of their houses specifically for drying coffee parchment. Keeping the beans off bare ground prevents earthy mold, catches steady mountain wind, and lets farmers cover the harvest quickly when afternoon rain rolls in.

brewingGuide.headline: Everyday Brewing Ratios.
brewingGuide.subtitle: Simple recipes we use to brew Dusun Gura coffee at home and in the shop.

methods.name: Indonesian Tubruk
steps: Put 12g of COGURA ground coffee into a warm mug.
Pour 180 ml of hot water (let boiling water sit for about 1 minute to drop to 93°C).
Stir gently 3-4 times, wait 4 minutes for the grounds to settle, and drink.

methods.name: V60 / Pour Over
steps: Rinse the paper filter with hot water, discard the rinse water, and add 15g of coffee.
Pour 30-40 ml of hot water to wet all the grounds and wait 30 seconds.
Pour the remaining water in stages up to 225 ml, finishing around 2 minutes 30 seconds.

methods.name: French Press / Drip
steps: Add 18g of coffee into your French Press or Vietnamese Drip brewer.
Pour 270 ml of 92°C hot water and gently stir the top layer.
Wait 4 minutes, press the plunger slowly, and pour straight into your cup.
